items.text: Roughly $2 trillion was wiped off the Nasdaq. According to Reuters, hedge funds locked in profits on 2026's AI winners ahead of year-end, while retail investors were the biggest net sellers since 2020. The break in volatility and risk appetite could shape pricing and liquidity into year-end.
items.title: AI sell-off hits Wall Street

items.text: CBS projects Democrats at 54 or more Senate seats, with a comfortable House majority expected. Trump said he would accept the results and use his veto; Speaker Johnson will not run again for the GOP leadership. On the agenda for markets: debt-ceiling talks, investigations and limits on Iran policy.
items.title: Democrats win both chambers of Congress

items.text: Brent rebounded 3.9% to near $98 after a roughly 9% drop the day before. Trump said there are no new strike plans but the US is ready to escalate; the NYT reports Iran is reviewing nuclear proposals brokered by Qatar. The risk of tanker attacks in the Gulf remains.
items.title: Iran war and oil

items.text: The Bank of England raised rates for the first time since 2023 and, with a hawkish vote split, left the door open to more. Markets pushed the Fed's next hike to March, pricing about 40 bp of further tightening over the cycle. Brazil paused its cuts; Mexico delivered a surprise cut.
items.title: Central banks tighten
